stories.title: Tiktoker 'super excited' to co-host BBC nature show
summary: Naturewatch, hosted by Chris Packham, Megan McCubbin and Kyle Thomas, is being made in Bristol.

stories.title: Prince William says UK faces terrifying risk of more wildfires due to climate change
summary: The prince says 2026 was the first summer he felt "worried about the scale of the wildfires".

stories.title: Trust vows to 'maintain spirit' of nature reserve
summary: Flatford Wildlife Garden is bought by the National Trust after being run by the RSPB for 15 years.

stories.title: Gene editing could replace a lifetime of medication, but there's a catch
summary: A single gene-editing treatment could someday protect against heart disease, high cholesterol, and other common conditions for decades, potentially replacing lifelong medications.
But scientists warn that permanently altering genes introduces risks that could take years to emerge, making long-term safety a critical challenge.

stories.title: Scientists trick cancer cells into making the drugs that kill them
summary: Scientists have developed a promising new cancer-fighting strategy that uses carbon monoxide naturally produced by tumor cells to manufacture powerful drugs inside the cancer cells themselves.
Early laboratory experiments suggest the technique could selectively attack cancer while sparing healthy cells, potentially paving the way for safer chemotherapy alternatives.

stories.title: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
summary: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha.
New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.

stories.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
summary: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain.

Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries.

These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.

stories.title: Action needed to tackle 'biodiversity crisis'
summary: The issue is part of wider concerns the government is not focused enough on the environment.

stories.title: Charity warns about damage of over-foraging fungi
summary: It says over-foraging, particularly in protected areas, damages habitats and wildlife.

stories.title: The brain’s hidden fear mechanism may explain anxiety and PTSD
summary: A surprising new discovery suggests that fear may cause the brain to blur the line between danger and safety rather than distinguish them more clearly.
By observing brain activity in mice using augmented reality, scientists found that memories of threatening and harmless environments began to overlap, potentially allowing faster responses to danger.
This "better safe than sorry" survival mechanism could help explain why people with anxiety or PTSD sometimes experience intense fear in completely safe situations.

stories.title: A 50-year-old mystery of vanishing frogs reveals a hidden killer
summary: A nearly 50-year-old mystery involving disappearing frogs in Brazil may finally be solved, with scientists uncovering evidence that a deadly fungus swept through the region and devastated vulnerable species.
Remarkably, many frog populations have since rebounded, suggesting they developed greater tolerance to the disease that once threatened their survival.

stories.title: Scientists identify two overlooked skills that predict reading success
summary: A massive new study reveals that intelligence plays a surprisingly limited role in children's reading success, while visual processing showed no meaningful connection at all.
Instead, the strongest predictors are sound recognition, vocabulary, and background knowledge, offering new clues about how to help struggling readers.

stories.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
summary: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago.
The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.

stories.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
summary: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock.
Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.

stories.title: Welsh public sector unlikely to meet net zero plans by 2030, say auditors
summary: A watchdog has criticised the lack of progress made by organisations in tackling climate change.

stories.title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK
summary: The government is launching the first study to measure PFAS in the UK population to understand the risks.

stories.title: AI data centres could undermine UK's emissions goals
summary: Four planned "hyperscale" data centres consider using gas-fired power for their electricity needs.

stories.title: Do the Shetland Isles need Cold War-style military protection?
summary: Calls are being made for the defence of the Shetland Isles to be strengthened after increased sightings of Russian trawlers off the coast of Scotland.

stories.title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored
summary: Researchers have detected signals from the smallest distances ever probed.

stories.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation.
Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

stories.title: Large Hadron Collider reveals evidence of Big Bang matter in surprisingly small collisions
summary: Scientists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have uncovered compelling new evidence that even relatively small atomic collisions can recreate the extraordinary state of matter that filled the universe moments after the Big Bang.

Known as quark-gluon plasma, this exotic substance forms at temperatures more than 100,000 times hotter than the center of the Sun, causing ordinary particles to break apart into their fundamental building blocks.

stories.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
summary: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two.
The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.

stories.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
summary: A surprising discovery suggests that rejuvenating the liver could help protect against Alzheimer’s disease and heart disease.
USC researchers found that an experimental drug restored aging liver cells in rats, cutting levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half and bringing bad cholesterol down to youthful levels.
The treatment also revived a previously unknown communication system that helps liver cells remove harmful substances from the bloodstream.
